title: Magic Lover's Murder Case
subtitle_source: /home/reo/Faks/GNN/case_closed/case_closed_dataset/subs_resolved/0132.txt, /home/reo/Faks/GNN/case_closed/case_closed_dataset/subs_resolved/0134.txt (0133 not read; two of the three episode transcripts read in full)
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Ran, Kogoro Mouri, Sonoko, Inspector Megure) omitted by convention. Katsuki Doito is kept as a node despite being a recurring franchise character (Kaito Kid in disguise) because he is central to this specific case's plot and reveal, not a background detective-cast regular. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved. case_type: murder. Online usernames are preserved as person attrs since the source explicitly plays on them (one is literally 'Red Herring'). 'Shadow Priest' was never a separate missing club member -- it was a second sockpuppet identity run by the culprit herself to fabricate a phantom suspect; this is captured as a clue plus an attr, not as its own person node, to avoid inventing a person the transcript explicitly says doesn't exist.

clues.desc: Hamano's body was found more than 10 meters from the lodge in undisturbed snow, with no footprints leading to or from it except those of the person who ran to check on him -- an apparently footprint-less, 'impossible' method of getting a body there.

The 'Shadow Priest' persona kept posting in the club's chat at the same time as 'The Fake Child' (Tanaka's handle) -- only possible if the same person ran both identities from separate phone lines, modems, and computers, meaning 'Shadow Priest' was never a separate, missing club member at all.

The club's 'random' leader-selection trick was performed with a blindfolded magician reading from papers marked in advance -- whoever prepared those papers and the ink-less pen controlled the outcome. The person 'randomly' assigned to heat the bath, gaining an unwitnessed roughly eight-minute window right before Hamano was killed, was also the one who had proposed the game and supplied its props.
